title: Cultivar Identity, Pedigree Integrity and Molecular Evidence

content.overview: Cannabis cultivar names are useful labels but are not substitutes for traceable genetic identity. Strong germplasm management combines source history, retained reference material, phenotype records and molecular evidence appropriate to the question being asked.

vocabulary.definition: Evidence describing whether samples are genetically the same, closely related or distinct at the markers or genomic regions examined.
Retained authenticated material used for later comparison of identity or performance.
Error or incomplete interpretation caused by relying on a genome reference that does not represent all diversity in a species or population.

sections.title: A name is metadata, not a genotype
sections.body: Commercial or historical names can be reused, renamed or attached to genetically different material. Breeding programs should preserve source and internal line IDs even when market names change.

sections.title: Markers answer limited questions
sections.body: A marker panel can estimate relatedness or test defined loci, but limited marker coverage does not prove complete genome identity or predict every phenotype.

sections.title: Pangenomic diversity changes interpretation
sections.body: Recent cannabis genomics emphasizes structural variation and reference bias. Broader genomic resources improve identity and trait analysis but still depend on sampling and validation.

workedExamples: Two plants sold under the same cultivar name may warrant internal IDs and molecular comparison before being treated as one breeding line.
A matching sex-linked marker does not prove two plants are otherwise genetically identical.
commonMistakes: Using cultivar names as proof of genetic identity.
Treating one marker as a whole-genome fingerprint.
Discarding original source and alias history after renaming a line.
content.practicalApplication: Maintain accession IDs, source, aliases, pedigree, retained references and molecular-test metadata together so identity evidence can be revisited as methods improve.
content.summary: Reliable genetic identity is cumulative evidence. Names, pedigrees, phenotype and molecular data each contribute different information.
